card.name: The word in in old historical prose
card.fires_on: The word "in" (occasionally "general" or "suddenly") in old-fashioned 19th-century narrative or essay prose, mostly before a time, place, or quantity phrase such as "in later times" or "in many places".

modes.label: In before time or place
modes.description: The word "in" introduces when or where something happened, in old historical writing about Mexico or similar topics.
modes.example: were much enlarged<< in>> the latter days of the empire, when

modes.label: Sentence-opening In
modes.description: A capitalised "In" begins a sentence that sums up a set of cases, as in "In all these cases".
modes.example: &c. &c.<< In>> all these cases the weights are expressed in

card.plain: It marks the little word "in" in old-style history and essay prose, just before a phrase of time, place, or scope.
